about:
# Beeline

*Formerly ForeverRoute. Same addon, new name: the command is `/bee`.*

Leveling routes for WoW Forever, 1 to 60, for all 56 race and class combinations, Alliance and Horde. A step card, an
arrow and map pins tell you what to accept, kill, hand in and train, and how to get to the next zone. Install it and
play: your plan loads by itself, quests you've already done are skipped, and it works at any level.

![The human paladin plan, 1 to 60](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/journey.gif)

## The card

**The next thing to do, always on screen.** It reads your quest log live, counts kills and loot, ticks steps off as you
play, and fits in hand-ins you finished early when you pass by. Skip a quest or a dungeon and the route keeps up.
The **?** on the card says why it picked a step, and the game's 3D navigation marker shows where to go. A rail down
the card's left side opens your route, Where to?, the side trips and the quest log check, each with its count (the
tab beside it folds it away).

![The card, step by step](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/card.gif)

## Pick your own zone

**Bored of a zone? Pick another.** "Where to?" (the signpost on the card's rail, or `/bee home`) lists the zones you could go to
now, with the XP each still has for you and the level that gets you to. Pick one and the route takes you there. If a
zone's quests need an earlier part you haven't done, those steps come first when they're close by, and a chain you
carry that's about to turn gray is pointed out before you leave. PLANNED NEXT takes you back to your plan, wherever
you wandered.

![Picking a zone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/where-to.gif)

## How the plans are made

Routes aren't hand-written. A planner builds them from the quest data and the game's own terrain, and every plan is
played from 1 to 60 by simulated players before it ships - including ones that wander off to other zones.

**It picks the next zone** by planning out every zone that fits your level:

![Choosing the next zone](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/planner-choice.gif)

**It keeps the quests worth doing**, and says why the rest were cut or left for later:

![Picking a zone's quests](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/quest-pick.gif)

**It finds the fastest way there** across one network of roads, boats, the tram, flights, class teleports and the
Skyborne skyship:

![Finding a trip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/travel.gif)

**Every plan, checked** - hours to 60, no grinding:

![Every plan, checked](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noopz/Beeline/main/docs/img/plans.gif)

## Getting started

Install Beeline from CurseForge or from [Releases](https://github.com/noopz/Beeline/releases) and log in.
The plan for your race and class loads by itself and starts you on the best part of it for your level and where you
are. Open any flight master's map once so the addon knows your flight paths.

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/bee` | Show or hide the card |
| `/bee list` | The Beeline window on your route (its sidebar has the rest: zones, side trips, log check) |
| `/bee home` | Home base - the zones you could go to now |
| `/bee dungeons` · `/bee class` · `/bee attune` · `/bee items` | Side trips: dungeons, class quests, attunements, special items |
| `/bee skip` · `/bee back` · `/bee undo` | Move through the steps by hand |
| `/bee logcheck` | Quests in your log the route won't use |
| `/bee why` | Why the addon did what it just did |
| `/bee report` | Copy a bug report to paste to us (anonymous) |
| `/bee news` | What changed in recent versions |
| `/bee options` | Settings |

What changed in each release: [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/noopz/Beeline/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). Something look wrong? `/bee report` and an issue here.

This repository holds the addon and its built-in plans. The planner that builds the plans and its simulator are not
public.

Beeline by noopz. [CC BY-NC-SA 4.0](https://github.com/noopz/Beeline/blob/main/LICENSE): share and adapt it with credit, never sell it. The quest data it is
built from is GPL-3.0 (QuestieDB); see [NOTICE](https://github.com/noopz/Beeline/blob/main/NOTICE). Contributions: [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/noopz/Beeline/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

releases.name: Beeline v3.4.0
releases.notes:
- Card: with one quest-log slot left, a hand-in out of town no longer has to wait for a pick-up in town first. The hand-in frees a slot, so the pick-up still has room when you pass back.
- A step that needs an item you left in the bank says so: "it's in your bank" on the card (a quest an item starts) and in a trip's Later list ("needs the Chained Essence of Eranikus in your bags (it's in your bank)"). The bank is the one you last opened.
- The route window's long steps wrap to two lines in the game too (3.3.0 cut them with "..."): the rows measured their text once, before the game had given the window a width.
- /bee report has a quest-items section: the items in your bags that start a quest, the items the card's step, the next five and its quest chain need, each as bags / bank / worn, and the chain's quests done or in your log. The bank is remembered when you open it (only quest items, per character), so a report sent away from the bank still says the Chained Essence of Eranikus is in it: The Essence of Eranikus's second part needs it with the Oathstone, and the report had no way to show it was banked. `node tools/report.js` prints the section with the items' and quests' names.
- Quest data: the items a quest hands you that a later one asks for (the Chained Essence of Eranikus, 160 of them) are known to the addon now (`ns.QUEST_ITEMS_HANDED`); the quest log check's "left over" list is unchanged.
- Farming, the card stays at the camp you are in. A gnome warlock killing Winterfall furbolgs by Donova Snowden in Winterspring was sent to Winterfall Village across the zone (by Moonglade) when a Den Watcher died at the camp: Threat of the Winterfall's Den Watchers are placed at the village. A kill now moves the card to the step placed nearest to where it counted, and a count for a step placed far away doesn't take the card off the kill step it holds where you are.
- Farming one quest's objectives at one camp, the card stays put. Deadwood of the North has its Avengers, Den Watchers and Shamans at one camp in Felwood: as your kills alternated, the card flipped between them at every other kill. The card now shows "Do these here" with a bar for each of them, and a kill for any of them keeps it where it is.
- The side rail's tab stays on a collapsed card. Clicking it opens the whole card with the rail; closing the rail with the tab folds the card back up. If you expand the card yourself meanwhile, the tab only closes the rail.
- The card's coordinates stay together: since the Later button widened a trip pick-up's buttons, "from Yorba Screwspigot · 67, 24" broke before the 24. A no-break space joins them now.
- The arrow no longer turns back to a zone crossing you have ridden past: a crossing counts as passed once you are beyond it toward the way's next point, even before the game says you are in the new zone. The Western Plaguelands / Eastern Plaguelands crossing lies on the Thondroril River, short of where the road enters Eastern Plaguelands, and the arrow, the game's waypoint and the map line pointed back west at it from 71.9, 58.4.
- A quest whose breadcrumb is in your log is no longer "not offered" by its giver. The giver lists it only once the breadcrumb is handed in, and the window you open to hand that in left the quest off your route with a chat line, then "offered after all" a moment later. This happened with Enraged Wildkin at Jaron Stoneshaper and Threat of the Winterfall at Donova Snowden (3.3.0 report, gnome warlock 55). The quest now waits for the hand-in.
- A flight path added close to a trip no longer becomes the card's step from far away. A hunter 53 back in the Western Plaguelands, whose Mount Hyjal steps waited for 54, was sent to the Bluebell flight path in Mount Hyjal on another continent. Stops added to the route also go in at or after your place in the plan, never into a stretch behind it.
- /bee report carries more of what happened: a line the addon logs again and again is counted on the first one ("(x14)") instead of filling the log. In 3.3.0 reports, 58% of the last 30 lines repeated an earlier one and pushed the useful ones out. A side quest you already have (The New Frontier, finished and in your log) is no longer "not offered: little XP" every two minutes at its giver. "No place on your route for Super Sticky Tar yet" is said once per route, not on every retry. The added stops are not logged again at each login under new step numbers. The flight-point line ("world map lists 1074 flight points") counts each point once and is said once per character.
- /bee report leaves out errors from an older build. A dev install is always version "dev", so an old error rode along in every report for a week: now only errors seen since the build you run are sent.
- Plans: the endgame of every plan is planned again from level 52. Up to there each plan is the same as before. The main Mount Hyjal visit now starts at 56, not 54: Hyjal's level-60 quests are offered only from 57, so a visit at 54 did about two-thirds of the zone and came back for the rest, and the Plaguelands' kill-and-collect quests filled the levels between. From 56 you finish mostly in Mount Hyjal and Winterspring: 77% (Alliance) and 71% (Horde) of the quest time from 55 to 60. Hours to 60 fall about 2% (Alliance 87.7 to 85.9, Horde 91.6 to 90.4).
- Plans: fewer bulk kill-and-collect quests from level 53, such as "Kill 20 Plaguehound Runt", "Kill 30 Plaguebat" and "Collect 50 Blackrock Medallion". The planner weighs their work extra when it picks a zone, and leaves out the ones that pay poorly for their time when other quests cover those levels. A quest whose drop rates the data doesn't know (most of Forever's new ones) is not left out on a guess. In the Plaguelands, bulk work from 53 drops from about 50 minutes to about 20 (Alliance) and 25 (Horde).
- Plans: The Good Stuff (20 Dark Iron Fanny Packs) is no longer on the Alliance main path in the Burning Steppes. Three Rugged Travelers there also drop the packs, which would take about 250 kills. A dungeon's item now comes from its dungeon unless the mobs outside can really give it, so the quest stays on the Blackrock Depths trip.
- Plans learn Mount Hyjal's Bluebell flight path in the Tainted Foothills. The planner missed her because her title is "Flight Mistress", and it kept only one flight master per zone.

releases.name: Beeline v3.3.0
releases.notes:
- The route window's header loses its line of hours, steps and level ("about 59 h left", "876 of 2679 steps done", "To level 60"): the hours were the plan's own estimate of a pace that isn't yours, the counts didn't fall as you handed quests in, and a built-in plan always goes to 60. Which build of the plan you're on is in the tooltip on its name.
- Sunken Temple trip: after you hand in The Essence of Eranikus at the Essence Font, the trip has a step to start its second part with the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight (its use button above the card; it needs the Chained Essence of Eranikus too, both go to Itharius). Without the Oathstone in your bags that quest and In Eranikus' Own Words wait under Later on this trip ("needs the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight in your bags") and the card moves on; they come back once you have it. On any trip, a pick-up whose earlier quests aren't handed in waits for them: the card no longer offered In Eranikus' Own Words with the quest before it never started.
- The card has a side rail down its left edge: your route, Where to? (a signpost), the side trips and the quest log check, a click each. Side trips carries a count of the trips left for you and Log check the quests in your log no route of yours uses; their tooltips break it down ("Side trips: 8 dungeons, 3 attunements, 1 class quest, 1 special reward", "Log check: 4 quests in your log no route of yours uses"). Options sit at its foot. The tab on the card's left edge folds the rail away and brings it back (it stays as you leave it); a collapsed card has neither. On a side trip, Back to plan heads the rail too.
- The card's top line names the route you are on: "Leveling · Azshara", "Home base · Westfall" for a zone you picked, or the side trip's name in its kind's colour.
- The house is gone from the card. Where to? on the rail opens the zones you could go to; Back to plan takes you off a side trip; "Back to level 60" stops finishing your quests at 60; a zone you picked that is done lists your plan's next zone first among its rows. The level-up line's button is the Where to? signpost. The hover bar keeps the flag, back, done, skip and collapse: the route list and options moved to the rail.
- The zones-ahead panel beside the card and its tab are gone: the route list (Route, on the rail) shows the zones ahead.
- Route list: a long step wraps to a second line instead of being cut off ("Hand in Dark Iron Legacy at Monument of Franclorn Forgewright (in Blackrock Depths)"), "..." only past the second line; the list still scrolls to its last step and opens on your current one. The quest log check's quest titles wrap to two lines too.
- On a dungeon trip or side trip the card walks only the pick-ups you can take now: your level allows them, and they are not red to you (5 or more levels above you, the quest log's own colour). The rest are Later on this trip: not walked, their follow-ups wait with them, and each comes back by itself when you reach its level, on this run of the trip or a later one. Nothing is cut from the trip. At 54 on Blackrock Depths: Kharan Mighthammer and The Fate of the Kingdom (level 59) come back at 55, Attunement to the Core (needs 55, level 60) and the Onyxia chain (Stormwind Rendezvous and 3 more) at 56. The side trips window lists them under the trip you are on, each by the level it comes back at.
- On a trip, a pick-up you can take now has a Later button beside its other buttons on the card: not this run. It comes back on your next level or your next start of that trip, its follow-ups wait with it, and the card moves on. It is not a skip: Undo brings it back, and the side trips window lists it under Later on this trip.
- Plans: every dungeon trip's pick-ups carry the level the game asks for them. Trips are planned at level 60, so a quest needing 55 had no level on it and was walked at 54. Dungeon trips regenerated for every plan.
- Trips fly only to flight paths you have. A level 55 who never took Mount Hyjal's Tainted Foothills flight path was told to fly there from Rut'theran Village, Moonglade and Everlook: "Mount Hyjal" was read as known because a flight path you have is in Stonetalon Mountains. The trip now flies to Everlook and rides on, and offers the Tainted Foothills flight path when you pass by.

releases.name: Beeline v3.2.3
releases.notes:
- Beeline has its own icon in the game's addon list (a bee in flight), on every Beeline addon: the plans, the walk maps and the detailed map line, not a question mark.
- Detailed map line: the run back to your corpse may drop off a cliff. A ghost can't die of a fall, so its line now takes the drops off ledges too high for the living (a zone's falls, read only on a corpse run): in Azshara, from the plateau at 71.2, 29.9 to the shore below it, the line is 183 yd instead of 1,500 round by the slope. The living's lines and memory are unchanged; a zone's mesh is 1-4% bigger, and up to 1 MB more is unpacked while you're a ghost (the Barrens). The rebuilt meshes also pass the audit on the current plans' walks in Dun Morogh, Searing Gorge, Stranglethorn Vale, Swamp of Sorrows, Desolace and Felwood, so those 6 zones have the detailed line now (43 of 49).

releases.name: Beeline v3.2.2
releases.notes: - Detailed map line: Feralas is back on it (37 zones). Its mesh had lost a steep hill path the plans walk (at 53, 52: the line went round for 2,000 yd where the walk is 940 yd); corners on steep hillsides that only a diagonal step crosses now join, in every zone outside the cities. Lines that swim to Feathermoon over the deep sea floor are no longer counted as going through walls: you swim at the surface. Every zone's mesh rebuilt; all 37 pass the audit on the 3.2.1 plans' walks (Feralas 60/60, Un'Goro 60/60).

releases.name: Beeline v3.2.1
releases.notes:
- Plans: the Timbermaw quests in Azshara that need Timbermaw Hold at Neutral (Report to Rageroar, Master Feardred, Toil and Trouble, Encroaching Corruption and 15 more) are off every built-in plan: the main route, the "go there instead" zone routes and the side trips. A character passing through Azshara at no standing could not take them (3.2.0 already keeps them off the card; now the plans no longer count on their XP).
- Horde plans rebuilt with 3.2.1's planner (no capital hops mid-zone, the walk to crossings priced like the addon's): about 0.9 hours less to 60 on average (91.6 h, from 92.5 h), every Horde plan 0.7 to 0.9 h less, simulated travel 34.8 h (35.0 h), no grinding. Alliance plans keep 3.1's route, reassembled the same way: the same hours to 60, simulated travel 30.6 h (30.8 h).
- Dungeon trips and side trips regenerated for every plan, so 3.2.0's trip wording reaches the built-in plans.
- Planner: its own trips (tools/travel.js) now price the walk to the crossings, flight masters and piers of your zone like the addon does since 3.1.2 (the walk maps' detours round mountains, not a straight line; a crossing reached only through another is no way round that one's enemy town), so the built-in plans' travel times match the trips the card gives you.
- Plans no longer fly you out of a zone in the middle of its quests to a capital and back for something that could wait for the end of the zone: the planner priced every flight inside a zone's route at 2 minutes, so a hand-in in Orgrimmar or the Undercity (Alliance Relations in Desolace, Notarized Claim in the Eastern Plaguelands) looked nearly free. A capital trip now happens mid-zone only when what comes after needs it (a follow-up that starts back in the zone, the level for the next quests). Class training waits for the end of the zone too, when you leave it within a level: no more flying from Stranglethorn to Stormwind and back at 44 for two ranks.
- Horde plans no longer send you to Ironforge to buy a Gyrochronatom for Gyro... What? (Badlands): the planner took any vendor of the item, of either faction.
- New planner check tools/capital-hops.js (run by tools/test-plan-lint.js): no main path of a built-in plan hops to a capital mid-zone when nothing after needs it, and none steps into the other faction's capitals; a visit of 10 or more of the city's own quests (Orgrimmar's at 18) and a class trip are not hops. 3.1.2's plans had 181 such hops and enemy-capital steps, 3.2.1's have 5, all in the race starts at levels 11-14 (a dwarf hunter's Stormwind errand from Dun Morogh, the orc and troll shamans' training and the tauren shaman's and warrior's Thunder Bluff hand-ins from the Barrens).
- Detailed map line: Feralas is off it again (the map keeps the plan's path there, as before 3.2.0). With the new plans' walks its mesh drew 8 lines through walls, most at Feathermoon Stronghold; 36 zones have it.
